style: Read this aloud warmly and clearly at a calm, gentle pace, like a kind TV weather reporter talking to a class of five-year-olds
lines: Happy. Sunny. When I feel happy, I smile and my body feels light and warm. What helps? Share it! Tell someone what made you happy.
Sad. Rainy. When I feel sad, my eyes get teary and my body feels heavy and slow. What helps? Talk to someone you trust, or ask for a hug. It is okay to cry.
Angry. Heat wave. When I feel angry, my face gets hot and my hands squeeze tight. What helps? Stop. Take three big, slow breaths. Count to ten.
Scared. Thunder and lightning. When I feel scared, my heart beats fast and I want to hide. What helps? Find a grown-up you trust. Hold something cozy.
Worried. Cloudy. When I feel worried, my tummy feels fluttery and my thoughts go round and round. What helps? Tell someone your worry. Make a plan together.
Confused. Foggy. When I feel confused, my head feels fuzzy and I am not sure what to do. What helps? Ask a question. Try again, slowly.
Excited. Windy. When I feel excited, my body wants to bounce and wiggle. What helps? Jump five times, then take a slow breath.
Calm. Gentle snow. When I feel calm, my body is still and my breathing is slow. What helps? Notice it! Remember this feeling for later.
Proud. Rainbow. When I feel proud, I stand tall and I want to show someone. What helps? Say: I did it! Tell a friend what you worked on.
Maya built a tall block tower. Then it fell down! How might Maya feel?
Tomorrow is Leo's birthday party! How might Leo feel?
Sam hears a loud BOOM of thunder in the middle of the night. How might Sam feel?
Ava rode her bike all by herself for the very first time. How might Ava feel?
Noah's friend grabbed his ball without asking. How might Noah feel?
It is Zoe's first day at a new school, and she does not know anyone yet. How might Zoe feel?
The teacher gave the directions, but Eli does not know what to do. How might Eli feel?
Mia's grandma is moving far away. How might Mia feel?
After recess, Jack lies on the rug and listens to soft music. How might Jack feel?
Priya gets a surprise letter in the mail from her cousin. How might Priya feel?
Ben's little brother keeps poking him in the car. How might Ben feel?
Lily finished the hardest puzzle in the classroom. How might Lily feel?
Happy.
Sad.
Angry.
Scared.
Worried.
Confused.
Excited.
Calm.
Proud.
That makes sense!
Feelings can be different!
We could say: "Want help building it again?"
We could say: "Happy birthday, Leo! What will you do?"
Sam could go find a grown-up and hold a cozy blanket.
We could say: "You did it, Ava! You kept trying."
Noah could take a breath and say: "Please ask first. Want to play together?"
We could say: "Hi Zoe! Want to sit with us?"
Eli could raise his hand and ask: "Can you say that again, please?"
We could say: "I'm sorry. Maybe you can draw her a picture."
Jack can remember this feeling for next time he feels wiggly.
We could say: "What did it say? Will you write back?"
Ben could say: "Please stop. I need some space."
We could say: "Wow, Lily! How did you figure it out?"
Thanks for sharing!
